posts.title: Honor Roll: Baugh, Montgomery and Lovett Collect SEC Weekly Awards After Ole Miss Rout
posts.contentText: Jadan Baugh (13) scores against Ole Miss as left tackle Bryce Lovett (53) stands over the play. Photo by Chris Spears, GatorBait Media. By GatorBait Media Staff The SEC office took a long look at Florida's 52-28 rout of No. 4 Ole Miss and handed out hardware to three Gators on Monday. Running back Jadan Baugh was named SEC Offensive Player of the Week, kick returner London Montgomery was named Special Teams Player of the Week and left tackle Bryce Lovett was named Offensive Lineman of the Week. It's the first career SEC weekly honor for all three. Baugh keeps rolling Baugh ran 29 times for 142 yards and three touchdowns against the Rebels and caught one pass for 12 yards. It was his fifth straight 100-yard rushing game, according to UF. He led all FBS players with 11 rushing first downs in Week 4, and UF credited him with 103 yards after contact. Baugh has run for at least 135 yards and multiple touchdowns in all four games this season. The junior leads the FBS in rushing touchdowns (11) and scoring. His 600 rushing yards are the most by a Gator through the first four games, according to UF. Montgomery flips the field Montgomery returned three kickoffs for 128 yards, an average of 42.7 per return. One kick after a 41-yard return in the third quarter, he broke a career-long 74-yarder. It was Florida's longest kickoff return since Solomon Patton went 100 yards at Missouri in 2013, according to UF, and Montgomery's 128 return yards are the most by an SEC player in a game this season. Jon Sumrall said Monday he nearly told the return team to take a touchback after an earlier miscue. “And then I was like, you know, I want to see London hit one,” he said. Lovett locks down the edge Lovett, making his fourth straight start at left tackle, played 69 snaps and did not allow a quarterback pressure or hurry, according to UF. He posted an 85.1 Pro Football Focus pass-blocking grade. Up front, Florida ran for 302 yards on 53 carries with six rushing touchdowns and did not allow a sack. It was the Gators' highest rushing total against an SEC opponent since they ran for 374 against South Carolina on Nov. 11, 2022. No. 8 Florida (4-0, 2-0 SEC) plays at No. 25 Missouri on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC.

posts.title: Pay the Toll: Sumrall Buries the Ole Miss Win, Braces for ‘Bloody Tuesday’ Before Missouri
posts.contentText: Jon Sumrall at the podium after Florida's 52-28 win over Ole Miss. Photo by Chris Spears, GatorBait Media. By GatorBait Media Staff Jon Sumrall has already moved on from the biggest win of his first season at Florida. He wants his players to do the same. “Told our team this morning, ‘I don’t want to hear anybody talk about that game the rest of the year,’” Sumrall said Monday, two days after No. 8 Florida ran over No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28. “If anybody brings it up in our building about what happened last week, I’m gonna be, like, livid because we have no control over that anymore. It’s gone.” He started the week with the film. “I’ve helped block it out for them this morning by showing them all the bad stuff we put on tape, too,” Sumrall said. “You have to humble yourself or you will be humbled.” Good news on VB3 The best news of the day was about wide receiver Vernell Brown III. “VB3, nothing serious,” Sumrall said. “Relative to what you could get, we got great news after the imaging and everything; the MRI revealed nothing that is long-term.” Sumrall called it “the lowest-grade strain you could get” and said Brown’s status for Saturday comes down to pain tolerance and confidence. “Medically, there’s nothing that’s going to hold him other than his own readiness,” he said. Bailey Stockton will be limited for much of the week with a sore back after what Sumrall described as “basically a car crash on the field with two guys,” though there is nothing structurally wrong. Dijon Johnson has a mild ankle injury, not a high-ankle sprain. “All of them, honestly, could be available this weekend,” Sumrall said. Eric Singleton Jr., who made a big impact late against Ole Miss, should be close to full speed. “I think Singleton’s going to be full-go this week,” Sumrall said. Bloody Tuesday Monday was a lighter helmets day, mostly inside. Tuesday is where Sumrall will find out whether the page has really turned. “Tomorrow we go outside the whole time, and it’s bloody Tuesday,” he said. “It’s like you gotta pay the toll. And so, if guys are ready to go pay the toll tomorrow, and compete and be physical … I feel like alright we got a shot.” Missouri starts up front Sumrall didn’t hide his respect for the No. 25 Tigers, especially their offensive line. “I think this is the best offensive line we’ve played,” he said. “We got our work cut out for us to win upfront this week.” He also pointed to Florida’s recent history in Columbia. “The last four trips we’ve gone to Missouri we’ve lost three of them,” Sumrall said. “So if we think it’s gonna be a freaking cake walk, I don’t care if it’s homecoming or whatever, we’re in for a rude awakening.” The Gators will lean again on quarterback Aaron Philo, whose steadiness has won over his coach. “Ever since Aaron’s arrival, he’s proved nothing but consistent, tough, dependable, reliable, great teammate,” Sumrall said. posts.title: BREAKING: MRI Confirms Grade 1 PCL Sprain for Gators WR Vernell Brown III
posts.contentText: By GatorBait Staff GAINESVILLE — Florida got the best news it could have hoped for on Vernell Brown III. An MRI confirmed the initial diagnosis of a Grade 1 PCL sprain in Brown’s knee, sources told GatorBait. Any knee injury involving a ligament brings real concern, so this result is about as good as the Gators could have expected. A Grade 1 sprain is the mildest grade. Sources say Brown shouldn’t miss many games, and possibly none at all. His return will depend on how his knee responds to treatment and how quickly it heals. Playing this weekend may be a bit ambitious, sources said, but the door isn’t closed. Brown, a sophomore from Gainesville, tweaked the knee late in the second quarter of Florida’s 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss on Saturday. Afterward, coach Jon Sumrall said, “Nothing’s … substantial, nothing’s like torn,” but called it too early to know about his availability. Brown leads the Gators with 17 catches for 271 yards and two touchdowns, according to the AP. Brown’s status will be one of the storylines to watch as No. 8 Florida gets ready for Saturday’s 3:30 p.m. ET game at No. 25 Missouri. GatorBait will have updates as they become available.

posts.title: 10 Thoughts From the Sidelines: Florida 52, Ole Miss 28
posts.contentText: Column | By Chris Spears, GatorBait Media Florida 52, Ole Miss 28. The scoreboard told you who won. The sideline told you what kind of team this is. 1. Florida has an identity again. The Gators want to run the football, and they want you to know it’s coming. Line up, lean on people and find out who still wants to tackle Jadan Baugh in the fourth quarter. Against the No. 4 team in the country, Florida ran for 302 yards. 2. Jadan Baugh is the compass. Twenty-nine carries, 142 yards, three touchdowns. That made five straight 100-yard games, a run only Emmitt Smith and Fred Taylor had put together at Florida. When the Gators need four yards, everybody in the stadium knows who’s getting the ball. He usually gets six. 3. Duke Clark means no intermission. You survive Baugh, he trots to the sideline, and in walks Duke Clark: 12 carries, 126 yards. That’s not a backup. That’s a second problem. His 45-yard touchdown came minutes after Ole Miss cut it to 17-14 and started to believe. “I thought Duke played out of his mind, and he’s got all the ability in the world.” — Jon Sumrall 4. Aaron Philo doesn't have to be the hero. Philo went 16 of 23 for 196 yards, threw a touchdown pass and ran for another. He didn’t try to win every snap. He won the next one. There’s maturity in handing it to No. 13 and getting out of the way. 5. This team takes a punch. Ole Miss punched back. It got tight twice, at 17-14 and again at 24-21, and nobody on Florida’s sideline blinked. The Gators answered with touchdowns on their first five possessions of the second half. Old Florida teams treated adversity like a warning. This one treats it like part of a Saturday. 6. Special teams were quietly loud. Right after Ole Miss pulled within 24-21, London Montgomery returned the kickoff 74 yards, and Florida needed three plays to score. He averaged 42.7 yards on three returns. Hidden yardage like that gets very visible by November. 7. The defense made the plays that mattered. It wasn’t a masterpiece. Trinidad Chambliss threw for 298 yards. But Jayden Woods’ strip-sack, recovered by Myles Graham, set up another touchdown and changed the temperature of the game. DJ Coleman added a fourth-quarter interception. Good defenses are judged by moments, and Florida’s showed up for them. 8. Vernell Brown III changes the shape of the field. His speed pushes safeties back and opens everything underneath for Baugh and Clark. He tweaked a knee late in the second quarter; Jon Sumrall said nothing is torn but it’s too early to know about next week. This offense is at its best with him on the field. Worth watching. Update, Sept. 27: An MRI confirmed a Grade 1 PCL sprain, the mildest grade, in Brown’s knee, sources told GatorBait. Read the latest. 9. The Swamp sounded like The Swamp. Third downs felt different. Big runs sounded different. The crowd didn’t come to be entertained; it came to take part. A real home-field advantage still makes 11 men play like 12. 10. Florida finished like it belongs. posts.title: Woods Chipper: Florida’s Defense, Special Teams Swing Win Over No. 4 Ole Miss
posts.contentText: GAINESVILLE — Trinidad Chambliss got his yards. Florida got the plays that decided the game. No. 21 Florida’s 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss on Saturday will be remembered for Jadan Baugh and Duke Clark each running for more than 100 yards. But the Gators’ defense and special teams tipped the night. Florida scored 31 of its 52 points on possessions that began with a fourth-down stop, a takeaway or a long return. Florida had no turnovers; Ole Miss had two. “There’s a handful of plays that swing it. And we made a lot of those critical plays tonight,” coach Jon Sumrall said after the game. Woods takes it away The biggest swing came late in the third quarter. Florida led 31-21, but Ole Miss had reached the Florida 40. On first-and-10 with 2:47 left in the quarter, Jayden Woods came off the edge, sacked Chambliss for a 3-yard loss and knocked the ball loose. Myles Graham recovered at the Florida 43. The Gators went 57 yards in seven plays, and Dallas Wilson’s 6-yard touchdown run early in the fourth quarter made it 38-21. “I just remember coming off the edge, I remember I tried to swipe. Didn’t quite hit. So I brought with a rip. Of course, like I’m taught. And then just ran the hoop,” Woods said. “And then as soon as I ran the hoop, I saw he was right there and his eyes were downfield, and first instinct is to go for the ball.” Woods said he “kind of blacked out” after he came off the edge. “Our offense was doing their thing all night. So I don’t want to credit it to just one play, but it was good to give the ball back to our offense,” Woods said. Fourth-and-1 sets the tone The first stop came on Ole Miss’ opening possession. Facing fourth-and-1 at its own 35, Ole Miss gave the ball to JT Lindsey, and Aaron Chiles dropped him for a 4-yard loss. Lindsey fumbled when Chiles hit him but fell on the ball, and Florida took over on downs at the Ole Miss 31. Three plays later, Patrick Durkin made a 49-yard field goal for a 10-0 lead. “I think that just ignited the stadium,” Sumrall said. “And unbelievable effort by our guys, Aaron Chiles and those guys that came in to make that stop.” Ole Miss did not score a touchdown in the first half, settling for two Lucas Carneiro field goals. By GatorBait’s count of ESPN’s play-by-play, the Rebels were 0-for-5 on third down before halftime. They finished 4-of-11. Woods called the defense’s approach “a bend but don’t break mentality.” Montgomery answers When Ole Miss got rolling after halftime, London Montgomery answered twice. Chambliss’ 8-yard touchdown run and two-point pass cut Florida’s lead to 17-14 early in the third quarter. Montgomery returned the kickoff 41 yards to the Florida 41, and four plays later Clark broke a 45-yard touchdown run. After Chambliss’ 10-yard touchdown run made it 24-21, Montgomery went 74 yards to the Ole Miss 26. Three plays later, Aaron Philo scored from a yard out. posts.title: Commit, Then Rout: Four-Star Safety Cyion Smith Picks Florida Before 52-28 Win Over No. 4 Ole Miss
posts.contentText: GAINESVILLE — Florida won twice Saturday: on the recruiting trail before kickoff, then 52-28 over No. 4 Ole Miss in front of Cyion Smith and a Swamp full of prospects. Smith, a four-star safety from Blountstown High in the Florida Panhandle, committed to the Gators hours before kickoff, Florida Gators On SI reported. He is the second commitment in Florida’s 2028 class, joining Hollywood Chaminade-Madonna four-star receiver Armani Strong. Smith (6-foot-2, 175 pounds) is the No. 279 overall prospect and No. 30 safety in the 2028 class in the Rivals Industry Ranking, which weights all the major recruiting services. Why Florida “Home. The coaches. Player development,” Smith told Rivals. “It was really a pretty easy decision. I have been feeling this way about Florida for a while.” Smith told Rivals he has been to Gainesville about four times since Jon Sumrall’s staff arrived, and that a summer 7-on-7 trip is when “Florida made a big move.” Safeties coach Chris Collins led the recruitment; Gators Online reported that Smith has talked with Collins almost every day since Florida offered in May, with Sumrall, defensive coordinator Brad White and Dae’one Wilkins also involved. “They really show they really want me, so they give me all they got,” Smith told Rivals. “I’m ready to give them all I got.” What he saw in The Swamp Smith plays safety, and the biggest defensive play of the night came from one. With Ole Miss at the Florida 22 late in the fourth quarter, Gators safety DJ Coleman intercepted Trinidad Chambliss at the 5. Florida forced two turnovers, a Jayden Woods sack-fumble that Myles Graham recovered and Coleman’s pick, and gave the ball away zero times. The offense did the rest. Jadan Baugh ran for 142 yards and three touchdowns, Duke Clark added 126 yards and a 45-yard touchdown, and Florida scored touchdowns on its first five possessions of the second half on the way to 302 rushing yards. Read the full game story. The final scoreboard in The Swamp: Florida 52, Ole Miss 28. (Photo by Chris Spears/GatorBait Media) A big weekend for Sumrall’s staff Florida hosted more than 70 prospects from the 2027, 2028 and 2029 classes for the Ole Miss game, according to Florida Gators On SI. Smith also held offers from Auburn, Miami, South Carolina and USF, according to his Rivals profile, and USA Today’s Vols Wire reported earlier this week that Tennessee had offered the former Mississippi State commitment. Florida’s 2028 class now has two pledges, and the Gators have a 4-0 start, a 2-0 SEC record and a win over a top-five team to sell. Next up: Florida at Missouri on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 3:30 p.m. ET.
